title: Typing into the selectbox doesn't search anymore after #15870
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary When typing into a selectbox, it is expected, that the existing content is cleared and search is started for a new element, which is matching to the typed content. Since 1.59.0 (probably #15870 ), this doesn't work anymore. Typing now adds text behind the current selection ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python ``` ### Steps To Reproduce _No response_ ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Current Behavior _No response_ ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.59.2 - Python version: 3.14 - Operating System: Windows - Browser: MS Edge ### Additional Information _No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15985)

### Analysis

This is a **frontend regression** in `st.selectbox`. When an option is already selected and the user starts typing, the committed label is no longer cleared — the typed characters are appended *after* the existing text (e.g. `United States` + `g` → `United Statesg`), so the fuzzy search matches nothing.

**Likely root cause:** `st.selectbox` was migrated from BaseWeb to react-aria's `ComboBox` in #15438. In the current implementation (`frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Dropdown/Selectbox.tsx`) the input is a controlled `inputValue` that is seeded with the committed value, and there is no select-all / clear-on-focus behavior (`handleInputPointerDown` only opens the dropdown). As a result, focusing the field places the caret in the existing text and new keystrokes insert at the caret instead of starting a fresh search — the old BaseWeb widget cleared the field on focus. A fix would likely add an `onFocus` handler that selects/clears the input text so the first keystroke replaces the selection.

**Note on #15870:** The reporter suspects #15870, but that PR only virtualized the dropdown *list rendering* (wrapping the `ListBox` in a `Virtualizer` and switching to the `items` render-prop API) and did not touch input/focus handling. #15870 also landed *after* the `1.59.0` tag (`1.59.0-2`, i.e. in `1.59.1`), whereas the react-aria migration (#15438) shipped in `1.59.0` — so the migration is the more probable origin of the behavior change reported "since 1.59.0". Worth confirming via bisect.

### Related Issues

- [#5240 — Impossible to highlight the selection text in `st.selectbox` to delete it all at once](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5240): Closest conceptual match — both are about the inability to clear/replace the committed selection text when the user wants to search for something new.
- [#15829 — Screen reader does not announce the list information on the combo box list item (Windows)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15829): Another recently reported bug in the newly migrated react-aria selectbox combobox (same component, also on Windows), useful for tracking migration follow-ups.
- [#12260 — Regression: Selectbox/Multiselect keyboard focus not activating on mobile](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12260): A related regression affecting typing/search entry into `st.selectbox` (mobile-specific), in the same "typing to search is broken" theme.
